title: The Problems with Proxies: Making Data Work Visible through Requester Practices

bias_targets.methodology: Qualitative semi-structured interviews and think-aloud sessions with 52 data work requesters, analyzing their use of 'English fluency' and 'native speaker' requirements as proxies to filter crowdworkers, which often unfairly excludes fluent non-native speakers.

Qualitative interviews identifying how requesters use location, time zone, and IP address filters to restrict data annotation tasks to residents of specific Western countries (e.g., US, UK, Australia, Canada).

Qualitative analysis of the systemic power dynamics and arbitrary evaluation proxies (e.g., approval ratings, task speed, attention checks) that disproportionately disadvantage and penalize low-wage, 'invisible collar' crowdworkers.
